classification: C. Historical artifact. The tick reconstruction removes the apparent straddle edge; the range expansion is real but not capturable by stop orders at these distances.
classification_text: The bar-level result came from three things the one-minute bars could not show: the spread at the release, the order in which the two stops are reached, and which side of the quote each stop lives on. At 15:30:00 server the Dukascopy spread is 0.86 ATR at the median, against a normal 0.25 ATR and a trigger distance of 0.25 ATR. The buy stop therefore sits inside the ask at the moment it is placed and fills on the first tick (median 98 ms), and the bid, which is where both the sell trigger and the long's stop live, is already at or below the sell level. Result on the 86 Thursday and Friday releases of 2025 downloaded: both sides touched in 92% of events, stop hit in 77%, net -0.76 ATR per event, and a mid-to-mid gross of -0.01 ATR, so there is no edge for costs to eat. The random same-day control loses less than the event.

Nothing in the frozen sensitivity set survives on development: triggers from 0.15 to 0.40 ATR lose 0.78 to 0.45 ATR per event (monotone with distance, never positive), every target from 0.5 to 1.5 ATR loses, every holding period gives the same number because the trade is decided in the first minute, and delaying the placement by 30 to 300 seconds after the release still loses, least at 120 seconds. The verdict is reached on development alone; the 2026 hold-out was not consulted (the chronological download had not reached it when this page was built), which the protocol permits for a rejection and forbids for an acceptance.

What is real: the first-minute bid-only range is 1.2 ATR at the median and the spread returns to normal within minutes. That is Report F's phenomenon, confirmed at tick level. It cannot be monetised by a symmetric stop straddle at any distance the plateau covered, because the instrument the straddle needs (a quote that is narrow at the moment of the move) does not exist at 8:30 New York on this feed, and on XM's feed the quoted spread is at least as wide.
spec_note: The specification was frozen from the Phase 13 code before any tick was read. Two changes relative to the bar code, both toward the brief's definitions: buy stops trigger and fill on the ask, sell stops on the bid, and the horizon was clipped to the tick hours downloaded (150 minutes after 15:30 for most days) because every trade resolved inside the first minutes; the plateau table shows the horizon makes no difference.
audit_notes: Dukascopy ticks carry millisecond UTC timestamps, converted to XM server time per day with the EU summer-time rule that the XM bars follow; the 15:30 event maps to 12:30 UTC in summer and 13:30 in winter, and the tick timestamps around the releases confirm the mapping (activity starts exactly at 15:30:00).

No duplicate timestamps, no bid above ask, no zero or negative spreads, three-decimal prices, sizes in millions of units. Tick gaps of 8 to 10 seconds occur in quiet minutes and never inside the event minute, which carries several hundred ticks.

The normal Dukascopy gold spread in the afternoon is about $0.55, comparable to XM's 51 points; its 99th percentile is $0.82 and its maximum $6.00, all at releases. This feed is an ECN aggregate, not XM's quote; XM's quoted spread at 15:30 in its own bars is 51 to 70 points, but a bar spread column cannot show a 300 ms spike, and no retail broker quotes a narrow spread at 8:30 New York.
Days whose event hour was not downloaded, and holidays without data (Good Friday 2025), are DATA_INSUFFICIENT, never filled in.
by_group: Thursday and Friday behave the same way; the weekday split that looked like a mechanism on bars was the ambiguous-minute share differing by day, not a directional or volatility difference the straddle could use. Monday to Wednesday were not downloaded; their bar-level result was flat and the tick mechanism is identical.
scenarios: Scenario A (fill at the triggering tick) is already negative; B and C make it worse in proportion to the fill delay; cancellation latency changes the number by a tenth of an ATR. The XM overlay adds nothing because the Dukascopy spread at the trigger already exceeds XM's 51 points. There is no fill assumption under which the frozen configuration is positive.
first_touch: Up-first at 90% is not directional information: it is the buy stop being pre-triggered by the widened ask. The conditional outcome after the first touch is a loss whichever side it is. The straddle therefore has neither directional nor usable volatility information at these distances; the volatility is real but arrives with a spread wider than the trigger.
windows: Almost every trigger occurs within the first second. The 1-to-5-second and later buckets are too small to say anything, which is itself the finding: the event is over before a stop order can be placed with any information.
toxicity: 59% of events are type 3 (both sides touched, stop inside 60 seconds) and 24% are type 4 (spread-driven trigger: the ask crosses the buy level while the mid does not). Clean triggers are 13% of events and lose too. The strategy is not losing because the event is bad; it is losing because the trigger is mechanically inside the spread at the only moment the move happens.
plateau: There is no plateau. Wider triggers lose less because fewer of them are inside the spread (0.15: -0.78, 0.40: -0.45), and the trend does not reach zero within the frozen range. Targets and horizons do not matter because the outcome is fixed in the first minute. The delayed-start row is the only variant that moves toward zero (best -0.13 at +120 seconds), and it is still negative on development, so it is not promoted.
controls: The random same-day straddle loses 0.15 ATR per attempt, the same order as the Phase 13 bar-level baseline; the 15:30 straddle loses five times more. The event is worse than random for this order type, which is the opposite of the bar-level picture.
cost: Gross mid-to-mid is negative, so there is no edge for costs to consume; the cost share is undefined rather than 80 to 90 percent. FRAGILE would be too kind a label.
next: Per the brief, outcome C: reject and return to the remaining missing-information hypotheses. No filter, wider trigger or delayed start is promoted from this study; the delayed-start row is recorded in the ledger as negative on development.

What the phenomenon still permits, as hypotheses for a later ledger entry, not as rescues: a directional bet on the release surprise (needs the calendar, Report D), or a limit-order design that provides liquidity into the spike instead of taking it; both are different mechanisms with their own frozen specs, not variants of this one.
The manual trade log remains the highest-value unmeasured dataset and needs no infrastructure.
Housekeeping: the tick files stay on D: (data/ticks) for the Report E microstructure work; the downloader script and the reconstruction are reusable for any other event window by changing the hours.
